## What does this mean?

Identify when ranking and reference evidence is trustworthy enough to use and when it needs review.

## Why does it matter?

Evidence reliability spans failure diagnosis, provenance, evaluation scope,
and escalation decisions for generated references and ranking signals.

## How does it work?

<ol class="hub-process hub-record-path">
<li class="hub-process-step"><strong>Questions</strong><br>3 questions defines what this theme is trying to learn.</li>
<li class="hub-process-step"><strong>Evidence</strong><br>8 studies records the current evidence.</li>
<li class="hub-process-step"><strong>Decision</strong><br>Iterate</li>
</ol>

## What do we know?

::: {.hub-conclusion}
### Current conclusion

Known failures cluster around ambiguity, evidence custody, and scope changes; selective review is warranted but no complete reliability predictor exists.
:::

**Practical decision**

Iterate

## What is missing?

**Confidence and evidence boundary**

Low confidence. Audits use purposive or known-failure samples and do not estimate hidden-test prevalence.

## Questions in this theme

<div class="hub-question-row">
<h3><a href="../../questions/failure-conditions.qmd">When do promising signals fail?</a></h3>
<p>Which request types, evidence gaps, and operational constraints make a ranking or reference method unreliable?</p>
<p><strong>Current bounded answer</strong><br>Failures cluster around ambiguity, entity resolution, evidence custody, scope changes, and over-tuned fusion, but no complete predictor exists.</p>
<p><strong>Still open</strong></p>
<ul>
<li>Can failure clusters be detected before a decision?</li>
<li>Can reliability-aware fusion improve without adding leakage?</li>
</ul>
</div>

<div class="hub-question-row">
<h3><a href="../../questions/reference-reliability.qmd">How reliable must a generated reference be?</a></h3>
<p>When a generated answer guides candidate comparison, when is it trustworthy enough and when should it be reviewed?</p>
<p><strong>Current bounded answer</strong><br>Gemini was the strongest reviewed default, but difficult and ambiguous cases still need selective escalation.</p>
<p><strong>Still open</strong></p>
<ul>
<li>Can a local judge reproduce the escalation set?</li>
<li>How often does grounding harm an initially good answer?</li>
</ul>
</div>

<div class="hub-question-row">
<h3><a href="../../questions/response-evidence.qmd">Can model responses provide useful ranking evidence?</a></h3>
<p>Does comparing a request or reference answer with candidate responses help choose the best models?</p>
<p><strong>Current bounded answer</strong><br>Direct lexical response retrieval underperformed; bounded refinement and reference-based paths have separate evidence.</p>
<p><strong>Still open</strong></p>
<ul>
<li>Can reliable references support a leakage-safe reranker?</li>
<li>Which response failures are predictable before ranking?</li>
</ul>
</div>
